newsitem.title: USA: Court dismisses Service Corp suit vs Loewen.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses Service Corp suit vs Loewen.

text.p: The Loewen Group Inc said on Sunday a Texas U.S. District Court granted its motion to dismiss the lawsuit Service Corp International filed a day before starting its hostile tender offer for Loewen.
The Texas federal court dismissed Service Corp's claim for a declaratory judgement, which sought to stop Loewen from bringing antitrust claims against Service Corp.

Houston-based Service Corp, the largest funeral services comany in North America, offered to buy Lowen for $2.9 billion. Loewen, a funeral services company based in Vancouver, is Service Corp's chief rival.

Loewen filed a lawsuit against Service Corp, alleging Service Corp's unsolicited bid would substantially reduce market competition. Several states have launched investigations into the potential antitrust implications of a deal.

Loewen said on Sunday the ruling of the Texas federal court cleared the way for it to proceed with its antitrust lawsuit in New York federal court, challenging the proposed business combination of Service Corp and Loewen.
Service Corp was not immediately available to comment.

The Texas federal court found Service Corp filed its lawsuit on the same day its board decided to make a proposed hostile exchange offer for Loewen's stock and before that proposed offer was made public or even made known to Loewen's principals, the company said.
